holidays.name: National Cold Cuts Day
holidays.description: A salute to sliced deli meats and the sandwiches they fill. Pile your rye high with turkey, ham, salami, and bologna, and consider it a patriotic duty.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food day. Its origins are murky, but it is widely listed on food holiday calendars and is mostly promoted by deli fans and food brands.
holidays.funFact: Bologna, a classic cold cut, takes its name from the Italian city of Bologna, whose famous mortadella was the inspiration for the American version.

holidays.name: World Wildlife Day
holidays.description: A global day to celebrate the planet's wild animals and plants and to raise awareness about the threats they face. Expect everything from pandas to pangolins to get their moment in the spotlight.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed it in 2013. March 3 was chosen because it is the anniversary of the signing of CITES, the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species, in 1973.
holidays.funFact: Each year has a theme, and the day is one of the most widely observed UN international days, with events held in countries around the world.

holidays.name: World Hearing Day
holidays.description: A day to promote ear health and prevent hearing loss. It is a good excuse to turn down your headphones and get your ears checked.
holidays.origin: The World Health Organization launched it in 2007 as International Ear Care Day and later renamed it World Hearing Day. The date is written 3/3, which is said to resemble two ears.
holidays.funFact: The WHO estimates that over a billion young people are at risk of hearing loss from unsafe listening habits like loud music through earbuds.

holidays.name: Hinamatsuri (Girls' Day / Doll Festival)
holidays.description: A Japanese festival where families display elaborate tiered platforms of ornamental dolls dressed in ancient imperial court costumes, and enjoy sweet treats like hishimochi and chirashi sushi.
holidays.origin: It grew out of ancient Heian-period Chinese-influenced purification rituals, in which paper dolls were thought to carry away bad spirits and misfortune. It evolved into the doll display tradition during the Edo period.
holidays.funFact: Superstition says that if the dolls are not put away promptly after the festival, the daughter of the house will marry late.

holidays.name: I Want You to Be Happy Day
holidays.description: A cheerful day for spreading happiness to others. You are encouraged to wish well for the people around you and do something kind to brighten their day.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance, widely listed on novelty holiday calendars, designed to encourage people to focus on the happiness of others rather than their own.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists have found that doing kind things for others often boosts the giver's own happiness as much as the receiver's.
